newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef traded higher early in the week on fairly good demand and generally moderate offerings, USDA said. Retail and HRI demand was fairly good for their immediate needs at the start of the trading period, but as the week progressed, demand became very slow.

Consequently, some chuck and loin cuts were trading lower to keep inventories current. Rib cuts also experienced somewhat the same conditions, fairly good demand, but at uneven price levels early, late in the trading period, steady to somewhat firmer undertones were noted.

Closely trimmed items traded at steady to lower price levels on fairly good demand, most items continued to be a good value especially against the regular boxed beef cuts. Beef trimmings were generally steady on mostly moderate demand and offerings.
Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were uneven, fed cattle grinds were generally higher, while the blended coarse ground items were steady at best.

For the week - Select and Choice rib primal steady to 2.00 higher; Select and Choice chuck primal steady to 3.00 lower; Select and Choice round primal generally steady; Select and Choice loin primal steady to 2.00 lower; Closely trimmed items steady to 1.00 lower; Beef trimmings generally steady; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items steady to 4.00 higher.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn $1.21 at $105.91; 700/850 Dn $0.95 at $104.95; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up $0.20 at $101.29; 700/850 Dn $0.28 at $100.02.

COW AND BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT The boneless beef market continues to be under a great deal of pressure as supplies were readily available and demand remained limited. The boneless beef traded sharply lower this week on very light demand and moderate to heavy offerings.

Cow carcasses remained lower in response to the declining boneless beef market. Furthermore, cow cuts market traded mostly lower this week on heavy offerings and very light seasonal demand. Tenderloins experienced the most decline this week due to very light demand. Utility carcasses 1.50 lower; Cutter weak to 1.50 lower. Fresh 90% boneless beef 5.50-7.00 lower; 85% 4.00-7.00 lower; 75% 2.50-3.00 lower; 65% generally 1.50 lower. The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, September 19, 1996 was estimated at 63.43 per cwt., down 3.85 from a week ago Friday.
